controls.tooltip: Spectral reduction amount in dB. Range 0-20, step 1.

controls.tooltip: Spectral smoothing factor. Range 0-100.

controls.tooltip: Spectral whitening factor. Range 0-100.

controls.label: Rescale
controls.tooltip: Output rescale factor. Range 0-12, step 1.

controls.label: SNRthresh
controls.tooltip: Post-processing SNR threshold. Range -10 to +10 dB, step 1.

controls.label: Attenuation Limit
controls.tooltip: Maximum noise attenuation in dB (0 = bypass, 100 = maximum). Default 100. Higher values suppress more noise but may clip speech peaks.

controls.label: Post-Filter Beta
controls.tooltip: Post-filter aggressiveness (0 = disabled, 0.30 = maximum). Default 0. Higher values reduce residual musical-noise artifacts but may over-attenuate consonants.

controls.label: Strength
controls.tooltip: Dry/wet blend. 0%% = bypass (filter runs but output = input), 100%% = full NR, 200%% = over-drive (phase-flip, destructive). Default 100%%.

controls.label: Aggressiveness
controls.tooltip: MMSE-Wiener oversubtraction factor. Higher = more attenuation on low-SNR bins; 1 = gentle, 4 = default, 20+ = underwater.

controls.label: Floor
controls.tooltip: Minimum Wiener gain per bin (x0.001). 0 = silence, 50 = -26 dB (default), 1000 = 0 dB, 2000 = amplify.

controls.label: Alpha
controls.tooltip: Decision-directed smoothing (x0.01). 0 = no smoothing (chattery), 92 = Ephraim-Malah classic (default), 100 = frozen prior SNR.

controls.label: Bias
controls.tooltip: Min-statistics noise-floor bias (x0.1). <10 = underestimate noise (less NR), 12 = default, >30 = overestimate (erodes signal). Nudge up if NR is weak, down if it eats speech.

controls.label: Gsmooth
controls.tooltip: Temporal gain smoothing (x0.01). 0 = instant (musical noise), 70 = balanced (default), 100 = frozen gain.

controls.label: Model
controls.tooltip: This preference remains editable while offline.

controls.label: Try again
controls.tooltip: Run the saved noise reduction choice again.

controls.label: Suppression
controls.tooltip: More-negative values permit stronger suppression. Higher values retain more of the original signal and noise.

controls.label: Position
controls.tooltip: Choose whether NNR runs before or after automatic gain control.

controls.label: Alpha
controls.tooltip: Shapes deep-filter gains below the alpha knee. A value of 1 leaves those gains unchanged; values above 1 deepen them, while values below 1 lift them.

controls.label: Alpha knee
controls.tooltip: Gain threshold below which Alpha reshapes the deep-filter response.

controls.label: Noise time
controls.tooltip: Time constant for input-power normalization before the neural network.

controls.label: Maximum gain
controls.tooltip: Maximum gain the neural stage may add.

controls.label: Attack
controls.tooltip: How quickly suppression engages. Zero uses the model response.

controls.label: Release

controls.label: Threshold
controls.tooltip:
Controls the detection threshold for impulse noise.
Lower = more aggressive (blanks weaker impulses too).
Higher = more conservative (only strong clicks get blanked).

controls.label: Transition
controls.tooltip:
Time to decrease/increase to/from zero amplitude around an
impulse. Controls how gradually the blanker fades in and out:
very short = crisp click; longer = gentler but audible.

controls.label: Lead
controls.tooltip:
Time at zero amplitude BEFORE the detected impulse. Blanks
the leading edge of the click that the detector would
otherwise miss. Raise slightly if clicks still get through.

controls.label: Lag
controls.tooltip:
Time to remain at zero amplitude AFTER the impulse. Blanks
the decay tail of the click. Raise this if pops still have
an audible ringing after the initial transient.

controls.label: NB2 Mode
controls.tooltip:
Method used to fill in the blanked samples when NB2 triggers.
Zero silences the impulse entirely; the other modes synthesise
a replacement waveform from surrounding samples to reduce
audible artifacts on voice peaks.

controls.label: Threshold 1
controls.tooltip:
Multiple of the running noise power at which a sample is
flagged as a candidate outlier. Lower = more aggressive
first-pass detection; higher = miss weaker noise.

controls.label: Threshold 2
controls.tooltip:
Multiplier applied to the final detection threshold. It confirms
candidates from Threshold 1 as real noise outliers. Lower =
more aggressive overall blanking; higher = fewer false triggers
on genuine voice peaks.

controls.label: Output Bandwidth
controls.tooltip:
Width of the audio band SNB operates on, centered on zero.
Smaller = focuses the blanker on the active passband;
larger = covers wider modes (FM, DRM). Default 6000 Hz
covers SSB + AM comfortably.
